question.text: The volcanoes Mount Pinatubo (pin-uh-TOO-boh) and Mount Mayon (mah-YAWN) are located on this island, the largest in the Philippines.
question.clue: This island, which sits to the south of the Babuyan Islands, is also home to the basin of the Cagayan River and Clark Air Base, which was heavily damaged by another of its volcanoes.

swap.leadin: This woman won the 1991 Nobel Peace Prize but could not accept it in person, as the ruling military junta held her under house arrest.
swap.text: Name this activist and politician who became State Counsellor of her country in 2016. Since her rise to power, she has been heavily criticized for her inaction against the persecution of the Rohingya people.
swap.answerHtml: Aung San Suu Kyi ([ong sahn soo chee], but be lenient) (prompt on “Suu” or “Kyi” alone)
swap.clue: This leader allegedly called two Reuters journalists "traitors" after they were arrested while investigating the Inn Din Massacre.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Southeast Asian independence movements.
question.text: David Marshall campaigned for the independence of this country. Reforms by its first leader, Lee Kwan Yew, made this city-state one of the four "Asian Tigers" with rapidly-growing economies.
question.clue: Colonial era leaders of this city negotiated with the Sultan of Johor for British control of this city, which was later the site of the largest military capitulation in British military history.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Asian political families.
swap.text: One member of this family dealt with the aftermath of Typhoon Haiyan in 2013. His mother Corazon's controversial 1986 election loss led to the People Power Revolution.
swap.clue: A member of this family, who was supported by Cardinal Sin, founded the Lakas ng Bayan Party and was assassinated at an airport which now bears his name.

question.leadin: Three wars were fought in the 19th century in this country in the name of British Imperialism.
question.text: Name this country home to the Irrawaddy Delta. Rangoon was the hub of the British-ruled "Lower" portion of this country.
question.clue: Lion statues from this country name long-range Chindit brigades.

swap.leadin: George Lambert helped provoke the second war between Britain and this country.
swap.text: Name this country, which fought three wars against the British Empire, culminating in the capture and looting of Mandalay. This country had previously been ruled by the Konbaung Dynasty.
swap.clue: Saya San was executed for leading a 1930 rebellion in this country, where colonial authorities frequented the Pegu Club.

question.leadin: Along with future vice president Mohamad Hatta, this leader declared his country's independence following the Japanese surrender in 1945 and he resisted Dutch re-colonization efforts.
question.text: Name this leader who aided in organizing the Bandung Conference, a precursor to the Non-Aligned Movement. This leader was a proponent of "Guided Democracy."
question.clue: His state philosophy was known as Pancasila, or Five Principles, and he was forced to declare his nationa's independence by a 1945 kidnapping.

swap.leadin: Answer the following questions about 20th century Asian dictators.
swap.text: This leader of the Khmer Rouge ruled as dictator of Cambodia between 1976 and 1979. His agrarian socialist policies and political purges killed over a million of his own people.
swap.clue: Relations between this man's government and its Eastern neighbor deteriorated during his rule, leading to a Vietnamese invasion that ousted him from power.

question.text: This city served as the capital of the Khmer Empire in present-day Cambodia. It is perhaps most famous for its Wat, which was built by King Suryavarman II.
question.clue: This site was constructed around a hill that was taken to represent the mythical Mount Meru.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about the influence of Sanskrit culture pretty far away from India.
swap.text: The past nine kings of this Southeast Asian country have used the name "Rama," after the mythical character. The British governess Anna Leonowens tutored one king of this nation.
swap.clue: This country was unified under the Thonburi Kingdom after the fall of the Ayutthaya Kingdom.

question.text: This leader of South Vietnam ousted the emperor Bao Dai and enjoyed U.S. support until 1963, when the loss of that support allowed for his assassination.
question.clue: This man overthrew the last Emperor Bao Dai ] in a fraudulent 1955 referendum, while a 1963 coup and siege of the Gia Long Palace led to his deposition and assassination.

swap.leadin: The death of a monarch with this name was initially ruled an accident despite shots to his back.
swap.text: Give this regnal name of Ananda Mahidol, whose predecessor was criticized during a 1932 constitutional revolution. All rulers of the Rattanakosin ("rat-tan-uh-KOH-sin") kingdom took on this regnal name.
swap.clue: The "Promoters" revolution, whose leaders included the dictator Phibun, overthrew a king with this regnal name in 1932.

question.text: General Harold Briggs approved the use of this chemical to destroy jungles during the Malayan Emergency. It was more famously used in the Vietnam War.
question.clue: This carcinogen and defoliant that the United States used in an attempt to increase the visibility of Viet Cong troops.

swap.text: Roel van Duyn, the founder of Provo, credits the offshoot group "Baastards" with leading the first Dutch protest against this conflict. Harold Wilson sent the Davies Mission to attempt to negotiate an end to this conflict.
swap.clue: The use of Agent Orange to defoliate trees during this conflict was controversial for its health effects on soldiers.

question.leadin: This man was the only monarch of the Thonburi Kingdom, in which role he subjugated the Lanna Kingdom and arranged for the burial of Ekatat, the last ruler of Ayyuthaya.
question.text: Name this revered king, who is sometimes de-legitimized for being partly of Teochew Chinese ancestry. He positive relations with Portugal, Britain, and Netherlands, receiving gifts of guns from each, but was killed by a friend who proceeded to establish the Chakri dynasty.
question.clue: This ruler stabilized the frontier by conquering the Lanna kingdom after leading a guerilla war to repel an occupation by the Konbaung ("kohn-baong") dynasty of Burma.

swap.text: This kingdom was founded by U Thong, and came to dominate much of Southeast Asia from the fourteenth to eighteenth centuries. Its last king, Ekathat, was defeated by the Burmese in the 1760s.
swap.clue: Under its King Naresuan, this dynasty defeated an Eastern invader at the Battle of Nong Sarai.

question.leadin: Along with purchasing the superyacht Equanimity, funds embezzled in this scandal were ironically used to finance Red Granite Pictures's production of The Wolf of Wall Street.
question.text: Name this scandal in which president Najib Razak and his conspirators siphoned billions from Malaysia's sovereign wealth fund.

swap.leadin: A ruler from this family often held court with his pet orangutan Betsy, and he once held a trial in which he sentenced a man-eating crocodile to "be instantly killed without honours."
swap.text: Name this royal family, whose rule began when Omar Ali Saifuddin II granted its patriarch territory around the modern-day city of Kuching and the region of Bau. As rulers, they were known as the "White Rajahs."

question.text: Following the fall of the Pagan empire, a new capital was established at this city, which would also serve as the capital of the Toungoo dynasty. The Konbaung dynasty's seat was also referred to as the "Court of" this city.
question.clue: Prior to the first war, the Konbaung Dynasty of Burma moved its capital to this city, which was the namesake of a dynasty that ruled from 1364 until its defeat by the southern Toungoo in the 16th century. British Upper Burma was sometimes called the kingdom of this city.

swap.leadin: It rose to power when its leader Anawrahta Minsaw subsumed the Thaton people, and its last ruler, the cowardly glutton Narathihapate, took poison after it lost the battle of Ngasaunggyan.
swap.text: Name this Theravada Buddhist kingdom that united the Irrawaddy river basin in the early 1000s AD.
swap.answerHtml: Pagan kingdom [buh-GAHN; do not accept or prompt “Burma”]
swap.clue: This kingdom began to form when cities such as Beikthano and Sri Ksetra of the Pyu people were invaded from the north by the Nanzhao kingdom, and began in earnest when the Mon capital of Thaton was taken by their first and greatest king, Anawrahta.
